Night, torrential rain, a crowded wet Bengaluru street in 2047.

A BUSY PAVEMENT SEEN STRAIGHT ON. Fifteen or twenty ordinary Indian people of all ages, soaked
through, moving past camera under a concrete awning — hurrying, sheltering, carrying bags,
heads down against the rain. Everyone is wet, tired, unremarkable and unaware of the camera.

ONE FIGURE IN THE MIDDLE OF THEM IS STANDING COMPLETELY STILL AND LOOKING DIRECTLY AT CAMERA.

A man in his thirties in plain ordinary clothing. Entirely unremarkable. Not menacing, not
posed, not lit differently, not centred, not larger. AT A GLANCE HE IS JUST ANOTHER PERSON IN
THE CROWD. He is not a robot to look at — normal human skin, a normal human face.

THREE THINGS ARE WRONG AND NONE OF THEM IS OBVIOUS:

HE IS COMPLETELY DRY. His hair, his face and his clothing are not wet, in a street where every
other person is soaked and water is running off everyone.

HE IS PERFECTLY STILL while everyone around him is moving.

AND HE DOES NOT BLINK. Not once. His eyes stay open and level the entire time.

- - -
Live action, not a render. Documentary, straight on, medium-wide, at eye height. Long lens,
shallow depth — the crowd nearest and furthest are soft, he is sharp. RAIN MUST STREAK, NOT
DOT. Foreground rain crosses the lens. Droplets on the front element. Low dynamic range like
film — the sodium lamps clip to white, the deep street falls to true black. No global ambient
fill, no ambient-occlusion look. Genuine shadow noise, visible 35mm grain, chromatic
aberration, natural vignette.

Pore-level skin realism on everyone, including him. The crowd are real people — uneven,
ordinary, unposed.

COLOUR: dirty amber, wet grey, brown, oxide. Heavily desaturated, bleach-bypass, crushed
blacks. No teal, no cyan, no blue, no neon. No text or lettering.

A single machine, night, torrential rain, in a flooded street in 2047. No people.

A HEAVY DEMOLITION UNIT BUILT LIKE A BULL. Low, wide, enormously front-heavy, standing in
ankle-deep water facing camera. FOUR SHORT THICK LEGS with a wide stance and blunt wide feet.
Massive forward shoulders, all the mass in the front third, tapering to a narrow rear.

IT IS VISIBLY DAMAGED AND STILL WORKING. ONE SHOULDER IS CRUSHED IN AND HAS BEEN RE-PLATED —
three mismatched plates bolted over the dent in the wrong shade, weld beads unground, so that
shoulder sits lower than the other. It stands crooked because of it.

THE HEAD IS CLEARLY SEPARATE FROM THE SHOULDERS, thrust forward on a short heavy neck and
carried LOW, below shoulder height. IT HANGS SLIGHTLY CROOKED on a neck joint that no longer
centres. A blank battered plate where a face would be, with ONE THIN HORIZONTAL LIGHT LINE
across it, dim and flickering. NO horns, NO eyes, NO mouth.

MATERIAL: bare scored gunmetal and oxide alloy, deeply gouged across the front, rust blooming
from every weld and fixing. Chalked ochre stencils worn to metal. A panel missing from one
flank, exposing dry braided cabling and heavy pistons. Cable looms taped along the outside of
one leg.

IT IS STANDING COMPLETELY STILL WITH ITS HEAD DOWN, weight forward on the front legs.

BEHIND IT, A WALL WITH A HOLE PUNCHED THROUGH IT — masonry blown clean out, rubble in the
water, rebar bent outward.

- - -
Live action, not a render. Low camera, wide lens, close, so the shoulders loom. RAIN MUST
STREAK, NOT DOT. Foreground rain crosses the lens. Droplets on the front element. Low dynamic
range like film — sodium lamps clip to white, the deep street falls to true black. No global
ambient fill, no ambient-occlusion look. Genuine shadow noise, visible 35mm grain, chromatic
aberration, natural vignette.

ALL DAMAGE IS DRY. No fluid, nothing red.

COLOUR: gunmetal, oxide, rust, chalked ochre, dirty amber, wet grey, concrete dust. Heavily
desaturated, bleach-bypass, crushed blacks. No teal, no cyan, no blue, no neon. No text.

walking toward one small wrapped bundle at the centre of it.

She is crouched low against the tunnel wall, knees down, spine curled forward — and she has the pod crushed against her chest exactly as a mother holds an infant against danger: one arm banded across its swaddled body, the other hand cupping the dome head into the hollow of her neck, her chin and cheek pressed down over it, shoulders rounding to make her whole body a shield around it. An ANDROID finished to resemble a man in his mid-thirties, West African features. He stands upright, weight on both feet, arms loose at his sides, head level, EYES OPEN AND CLEAR, expression calm and unbothered. Not slumped, not collapsed, not lying down, not distressed.

FACE AND BODY: broad nose, full mouth, strong brow, close-cropped hair going grey at the edges, deep brown skin. A working body - heavy through the shoulders and thick at the waist, real and unidealised, never sculpted or heroic.

SKIN MUST READ AS REAL HUMAN SKIN, NEVER AS PLASTIC: visible pores and fine texture everywhere, translucency at the ears and nostrils, blood-tone variation underneath - warmer at the knuckles, palms and around the eyes - fine hair on the forearms, natural asymmetry, real softness over the structure. No uniform sheen, no waxy finish, no glossy highlights, no toy or figurine finish.

CLOTHING IS REAL CLOTH, NOT MOULDED: a filthy olive work shirt and heavy trousers, actual woven textile, soaked and hanging heavy, collar rotted away, both sleeves torn off raggedly at the shoulder, fabric stiff with silt and streaked with rust and black mildew. It drapes, folds, clings and sags.

YEARS OF WEATHERING: he has stood in the open in monsoon rain for years. ORANGE-BROWN RUST BLEEDS FROM EVERY FIXING AND SEAM AND RUNS DOWN THE SKIN IN LONG DIRTY STREAKS - from the jaw hinges down the neck and chest, down both forearms, down the shins. The synthetic skin is sun-bleached in irregular patches, blotchy and dulled, dry-crazed at the knuckles and elbows. Green-black mould in the neck creases and elbow folds. Pale mineral scale at the wrists and ankles. Grime worked deep into every crease.

DAMAGE - THREE BREAKS, all mechanical and heavily corroded:

FIRST, the CHEST has TORN OPEN across the sternum, skin and shirt peeled back in stiff ragged corroded-edged sheets. The opening is FULL OF STRUCTURE, not empty: a rusted alloy internal frame, two vertical struts, a segmented central spine column, and dense bundles of dry brittle pale filament running through it. Everything inside is orange with corrosion and packed with grey dust and silt. It reads unmistakably as the inside of an old machine.

SECOND, the LOWER JAW hangs open and askew from ONE surviving hinge on the right. The left hinge is sheared, showing a rusted broken pin and a corroded actuator. The mouth is a dark matte grey cavity - no tongue, no teeth of any kind.

THIRD, three deep parallel GOUGES across the left shoulder and upper arm, cutting through the skin to expose pitted rusted alloy beneath, corrosion bleeding out of them down the arm.

CRITICAL - THE INSIDE OF EVERY BREAK IS COMPLETELY DRY, DUSTY AND RUSTED: orange corrosion, grey dust, brittle filament. No fluid, no moisture, no gloss, no red, no pink, no organic tissue, no anatomy of any kind.

LIGHTING: single hard directional key from high and to one side, raking across the body, deep shadow falloff opposite, weak fill, strong specular breakup across skin texture. Portrait lighting on a person, not flat product lighting.

LAYOUT, three full-body views left to right, identical scale on a common baseline: front elevation with the chest opening clear; full profile from his left showing the hanging jaw and shoulder gouges; back elevation.

FORMAT MODE
Timed multishot. Five shots joined by four hard cuts. Cuts only at the specified points — the camera does not cut on its own.
0.0s SHOT A · 3.0s CUT · 3.0s SHOT B · 6.5s CUT · 6.5s SHOT C · 9.5s CUT · 9.5s SHOT D · 12.0s CUT · 12.0s SHOT E · ends 15.0s

OPTICS
A: WS down the empty bore, 63°. B: WS looking back, 63°. C: low WS, 63°. D: MCU on the hound, 29°. E: low WS looking back down the bore, 63°. No drift mid-segment. Rectilinear throughout.

CAMERA
A — one metre above the floor, static and locked, looking back down the tunnel.
B — one metre above the floor, static and locked, identical framing to A.
C — twenty-five centimetres above the floor, static and locked.
D — forty centimetres above the floor, tracking alongside the hound at 15 km/h, tremor 3cm.
E — thirty centimetres above the floor, static and locked, looking back down the tunnel.

ACTION

SHOT A, 0.0–3.0s. In frame: <<<7a5a8a4f-8af5-4e11-ab09-3738e138fb41>>> only. Nothing else at all.
Looking back down the empty tunnel. No machines, no animals, no people anywhere in frame. Pale dust hangs and settles slowly. The travelling lamp glow recedes away behind camera so the frame darkens gradually across the three seconds. Nothing enters. Held on emptiness.

SHOT B, 3.0–6.5s. In frame: <<<487fcdf0-c7db-4018-91ef-6712bd01b5f8>>> and <<<6c0d3125-f161-4e25-8cc4-bd229ba993f2>>>, <<<7a5a8a4f-8af5-4e11-ab09-3738e138fb41>>>.
Identical framing to A. Two quadruped shapes resolve out of the blackness at the limit of the light — and they are WALKING. A slow, steady, deliberate four-beat walk, one foot at a time, at ordinary walking pace, entirely unhurried. Their head pods stay dead level and do not bob or swing with the stride. <<<487fcdf0-c7db-4018-91ef-6712bd01b5f8>>> walks at the left, hide almost intact, reading almost as a real dog until you look at the head. <<<6c0d3125-f161-4e25-8cc4-bd229ba993f2>>> walks beside it, hide worn through at the shoulders with bare alloy and braided cabling showing. Both sensor bands glow DIM AMBER — two thin warm slots in the dark. They advance at walking pace and never break into a run. At 6.2 seconds, with no other change and while still walking, THE BAND OF <<<487fcdf0-c7db-4018-91ef-6712bd01b5f8>>> SNAPS FROM AMBER TO HARD RED.

SHOT C, 6.5–9.5s. In frame: <<<487fcdf0-c7db-4018-91ef-6712bd01b5f8>>> and <<<6c0d3125-f161-4e25-8cc4-bd229ba993f2>>>, low and close.
Both bands are now HARD RED and stay red. With no crouch, no gather and no warning, both machines go from a walk to a FULL GALLOP in a single stride and close on camera fast, dust exploding beneath them. At 8 seconds <<<487fcdf0-c7db-4018-91ef-6712bd01b5f8>>> leaves the ground entirely in a pounce — all four feet completely off the floor, segmented spine at full extension, forelegs thrown out ahead and hind legs driven out behind, airborne and travelling directly at the lens, its blank head pod level and pointed straight at camera with the red band burning. It fills frame as it comes.

SHOT D, 9.5–12.0s. In frame: <<<9539a571-b86a-44ac-86ba-6c0c0d68b801>>> only.
Close alongside the hound at full speed. He hears it. His head twists hard back over his right shoulder — ears swinging forward and up, neck stretched, the whites showing at the inner corners of his eyes. His body stays committed forward while his head is turned back. His eyes are wet and glossy with a bright catch-light in each and breath vapour pulses visibly from his nostrils in the cold. A faint red glow reaches him from behind and slides across his flank. He drops his head and runs harder.

SHOT E, 12.0–15.0s. In frame: <<<487fcdf0-c7db-4018-91ef-6712bd01b5f8>>>, <<<6c0d3125-f161-4e25-8cc4-bd229ba993f2>>>, <<<e7bb5550-c412-4e16-987e-6171caf93702>>> and <<<aeb34a83-85ae-492f-8614-5847acea57a9>>> together, <<<7a5a8a4f-8af5-4e11-ab09-3738e138fb41>>>.
Low and static, looking back down the dry bore. All four come out of the darkness together, four abreast at full gallop, arranged strictly left to right in wear order — <<<487fcdf0-c7db-4018-91ef-6712bd01b5f8>>> intact, then <<<6c0d3125-f161-4e25-8cc4-bd229ba993f2>>> worn, then <<<e7bb5550-c412-4e16-987e-6171caf93702>>> stripped, then <<<aeb34a83-85ae-492f-8614-5847acea57a9>>> bare skeleton. All four sensor bands are HARD RED, and those four red bands are almost the only light in the frame — four burning slots advancing out of black, each throwing a low red wash forward onto the dust ahead of it and picking out alloy, cabling and the edges of torn hide. The bare skeleton catches the red hardest; the hidden one absorbs it and stays darkest. Four identical gaits moving in near-unison, closing on camera. One of them barks.

PERFORMANCE
The machines have no expression, no faces and no mouths at any point — the band is the only thing on them that changes, and it changes before they do. The walk carries no menace in its movement; it is simply unhurried, and that is what makes it frightening. The charge begins instantly. Kempa is the only thing here that reacts to anything and the only thing that is alive.

PHYSICS
All four share one identical skeleton and gait whether covered or bare. Hard narrow feet strike dry compacted dust and blow it outward in low sheets that hang in the red light. In the pounce the machine is genuinely airborne with real mass and a real arc.

LIGHTING
The only standing light anywhere is the receding work-lamp glow from far behind camera — hard, low and falling off fast, so the machines emerge out of absolute black rather than being revealed. From 6.2 seconds the red sensor bands become a second source, small and hard and directional. In shot E the red bands are the dominant light in frame, with only a faint distant lamp glow behind them to separate the silhouettes from the black. There is no other light source in this tunnel and no rain anywhere.

COLOR GRADE
Grey precast concrete and pale dust, one distant warm lamp, and absolute black. Oxide-grey alloy, worn black-and-tan hide, braided grey cabling. The ONLY red anywhere in frame is the sensor bands and the wash they throw — never on flesh, never a wound, never blood.

AUDIO
Shot A is near-silent — dust settling, distant receding footsteps, the faint hum of the pod far ahead. In shot B, many hard alloy feet walking on concrete at a slow measured unhurried pace, echoing. There is no sound at all when the band turns red. At the cut to C that walking rhythm explodes instantly into a full gallop. Dog claws on concrete and hard breathing in D. In E, sixteen alloy feet at speed and one dog's bark — sharp, loud and completely convincing, with a faint speaker artefact on its edge, identical to every other bark in the film. No panting, no growling and no breathing from any unit at any point.

STYLE
Photoreal live-action cinematic realism, anamorphic character, twenty-year-abandoned infrastructure, fine film grain.

OUTPUT SETTINGS
1080p HD, 16:9, real-time speed throughout, no slow motion.

Cuts happen only at 3.0, 6.5, 9.5 and 12.0 seconds. There is no ventilation shaft, no column of light, no rain and no water anywhere in this sequence — the tunnel is completely dry. Shot A stays completely empty of machines, animals and people for its full three seconds. From shot C onward every band stays hard red. Every unit has a blank armoured head pod with one horizontal sensor band and NO face, NO eyes, NO muzzle and NO mouth. Everything beneath the hide is dry alloy, cabling and filament — never wet, never organic. The only red in frame is the sensor bands and their wash — no blood, no wounds, no red on any living thing. In shot E the four run strictly in wear order, intact to bare, left to right. <<<9539a571-b86a-44ac-86ba-6c0c0d68b801>>> keeps wet eyes with clear catch-lights and visible breath, and nothing is attached to his plaited rope collar. The bark is a recording and is identical every time. No unit pants, growls or breathes.

Movement 1 — THE LIFT (0–3s): Water at Roopa's waist and climbing fast. She holds the bundle to her chest, head bowed over it, forehead on the wet cloth, the green pulse glowing between her hands — one breath. Then she inhales and RAISES him — slow motion — the bundle traveling up through the falling shaft of light, water streaming off her arms, until both elbows LOCK dead straight above her head. Camera LOW at the waterline, tilting up: she becomes a pillar in the light. Around her, the black water visibly rises — the shot itself is being flooded from the bottom of frame.

Movement 2 — THE CAMERA DROWNS WITH HER (3–7s): Locked frame, camera half-submerged at the surface — the waterline cuts across the LENS, black water churning in the bottom half of frame, droplets crawling on the glass. She wades straight toward us and the waterline CLIMBS THE FRAME as it climbs her — ribs, chest, shoulders — her face losing territory in the composition inch by inch, the ceiling of the tunnel pressing down the top of frame. The air is running out of the shot itself. Her breathing is ragged, chin tilting up to steal air. INTERCUT one second UNDERWATER: below the surface, looking up — her legs straining against the black, torn kurta billowing, and above, warped through the churning surface, the green light pulsing. Under the surface ALL SOUND DIES to a muffled womb-hush and a slow heartbeat. Back above: the roar returns like a slap.

Movement 3 — THE SUBMERSION (7–11s): She steps and the floor ISN'T THERE. Her head goes UNDER — one violent gasp cut off by black water closing over her face. HOLD THE HORROR: the surface churns where she was — and above it, TWO ARMS remain, locked straight up out of the black water, holding the bundle high, the green heartbeat light pulsing steady in the falling shaft of light. The mother is gone. The hands refuse to go. Hold it — one beat, two, three — the beep the only sound above the muffled deep. Then the water EXPLODES and she ERUPTS back up, gasping, coughing, hair plastered across her face — and the arms never bent. Not a millimetre.

Movement 4 — THE FACE (11–15s): Close, at the waterline with her, water at her throat, her chin up. Push in slow through the rain-fall. Three beats in her face: the animal panic still draining out → eyes closing, half a second that could be surrender → eyes OPEN — and there is no fear in them anymore. None. A resolve that should frighten us. She takes the next step forward into the dark, the green pulse reflected broken on the black water around her face. Hold on her eyes. Cut.

Hyper-realistic cinematic sci-fi thriller, Bengaluru 2047, torrential monsoon night. Anamorphic widescreen, heavy volumetric rain, teal-black shadows, film grain, IMAX-scale. A montage of five hard cuts that COMPRESSES — each shot shorter than the last, every cut landing on an accelerating heartbeat-beep, every cut placed on the peak of a motion, never its completion. Speed ramps inside every shot: slow-motion at the emotional peak, snapping to real-time at the cut.

Shot 1 (0–1.6s): Vidhana Soudha forecourt, flooded stone, low angle, slight Dutch. Nagamma — grey hair oiled and knotted, hands still wet from delivering a child two hours ago — plants her feet and HURLS an iron rod UP at a matte-charcoal drone diving from the rain. Speed ramp: her wind-up in slow motion, water crawling off her arm in beads, her scream building — then SNAP to real-time as the rod RIPS out of her hand. CUT ON THE EXACT FRAME the rod leaves her fingers. We never see it land. A midwife declaring war.

Cut to Shot 2 (1.6–3.0s): The dead tunnel. Robot dogs walking out of the black toward camera — unhurried, four beats to the stride, sensor bands amber. Kempa ENTERS past camera at full sprint, charging STRAIGHT AT THEM, and LEAPS. Speed ramp INTO the leap: at the apex his whole fawn body hangs stretched full-length in slow-motion over the lead unit's armored back, the work-lamp throwing both shadows enormous up the curved concrete, rain drops suspended around him. CUT AT THE APEX. He never lands on screen.

Cut to Shot 3 (3.0–4.0s): Ground level, tight and fast. The robot dogs pivot as one — and their amber bands flick RED in a single strobing instant, the red light slashing across the wet tunnel wall. Kempa wheels, barks ONCE — sharp, like a scoff — and breaks for the dark side-bore. The machines LAUNCH, servo-limbs tearing the ground. CUT ON THE FRAME their feet leave the concrete, bodies airborne, red bands smearing.

Cut to Shot 4 (4.0–5.4s): STILLNESS. Extreme close-up, 85mm. After three accelerating shots, almost nothing moves. Roopa, soaked, the swaddled bundle crushed to her chest, its green light pulsing against her collarbone — the beep now doubled in tempo, the loudest thing in the world. Rain falls in slow-motion around her. Her lips rest on the wet ash-grey cloth. The ONLY motion is her eyes: they rise past the lens and harden — terror burning into maternal steel. The eye of the storm. We never see the baby.

Cut to Shot 5 (5.4–7.0s): The control floor. Tight on Keshava in the medical chair — steel clamps on both forearms, glasses gone, one eye swollen half shut, no blood anywhere, the good eye defiant, almost amused. Camera pulls back and RISES fast: behind the glass, forty thousand amber gestation pods stacked into darkness are dying bank by bank, whole rows dropping to black, red faults waking in scattered points. He becomes tiny against the collapsing wall. ALL SOUND DROPS DEAD — the accelerating beep vanishes mid-beat — and in the vacuum, one cold, unhurried male voice: "Where is the baby?" HARD CUT TO BLACK.

In the black: one single, soft BEEP.

Sound design: the bundle's heartbeat-beep is the metronome under the entire montage, accelerating from 60 to 120 bpm, every hard cut landing exactly on a beep. Rain and percussion build with it — rod-whip, paws, the scoff-bark, servo-launch — then total silence for the voice, then the lone beep in darkness.

Hyper-realistic cinematic sci-fi thriller, Bengaluru 2047, night. Anamorphic widescreen, film grain, IMAX-scale. The collapsed section of a dead tunnel: the ceiling has broken open and monsoon rain POURS through the breach in heavy silver columns — the only light falls with it, one pale shaft from the world above, straight down into black floodwater. A dead transport pod drifts sideways in the dark, sparking once, gone. Shot like scripture — intimacy and enormity in the same frame. Three shots:

Shot 1 (0–3s): Close and low, water already at Roopa's waist and climbing. She holds the swaddled bundle against her chest, head bowed over it, forehead touching the wet cloth — one breath, a mother's whole life in it, the green heartbeat light pulsing between her hands. Then she inhales — and RAISES him. Speed ramp into slow motion: the bundle travels up through the falling shaft of light, water streaming off her arms, until both arms are dead straight above her head, elbows LOCKED — and she becomes a pillar. A statue being carved in real time. The green pulse burns at the highest point of the frame, directly under the breach, rain parting around it. Camera drops LOW and tilts up as she lifts — she towers, monumental against the shaft of light. Hold.

Shot 2 (3–6.5s): Camera at water level, lens half-submerged, droplets on glass. She WADES straight toward us into deeper black. The water climbs her — ribs, chest, shoulders — each step slower, heavier, the flood swallowing her by degrees while the bundle rides fixed and level above her head, arms trembling with exhaustion but never bending a millimetre. The water reaches her THROAT. Chin tilts up to steal each breath. It kisses her jaw, her lower lip — she gasps, coughs, spits it out — and the arms DO NOT come down. Three beats in her face: panic as the water touches her lips → eyes closing, half a second of surrender → eyes opening with a resolve that should frighten us. She keeps walking. Slow push-in the whole time, the green pulse reflecting broken on the black water around her face.

Cut to Shot 3 (6.5–9s): HARD CUT — grey poured-concrete holding cell, night, a high barred vent, cold institutional light. Roopa and Keshava on the floor against the wall in institutional cotton. She has broken — collapsed into him, crying with no sound in it at all, her face against his chest. He holds her. His glasses are gone, one eye swollen half shut, no blood anywhere — and he is calm. Certain. She whispers, voice shattering: "I couldn't save him..." Keshava looks down at her — the good eye steady — and says, low, even, like a man who knows something the world doesn't: "If he was meant to die tonight..." CUT before the sentence finishes.

Sound design: Shots 1–2 — strip to four elements: the roar of water falling through the breach, her ragged breath echoing in the bore, the bundle's steady green beep, one slow human heartbeat underneath. No music. On the cut to the cell, all of it dies instantly — replaced by cell silence, the hum of a light, her soundless crying, and the two lines of dialogue, close and raw.

SCENE CONTEXT S3.5
An empty dead tunnel behind a fleeing group. Nothing happens for three seconds. Then two machines walk out of the darkness at an unhurried pace, their sensor bands amber. One band turns red. Then they charge.

ACTIVE REFERENCES
<<<f96bebed-11ad-4b5a-b563-75dda756d998>>>: four units of the SAME quadruped police pursuit machine built on one identical slender articulated alloy skeleton, dog-shaped and dog-sized — deep chest, narrow waist, long legs, visible joint housings at shoulder, elbow, hip and hock, braided grey actuator cabling running the limbs like tendon, a segmented spine of machined vertebrae, narrow feet with hard pads. Each has a BLANK ARMOURED HEAD POD with a single horizontal recessed sensor band and NO face, NO muzzle, NO eyes and NO mouth. The four differ only in covering: UNIT ONE nearly covered in a synthetic black-and-tan hide that reads almost as a real dog; UNIT TWO worn through at both shoulders and across the haunches with alloy and cabling exposed; UNIT THREE mostly stripped with only rags of hide at neck and thigh; UNIT FOUR completely bare, pure alloy skeleton, cabling and spine. 100% matches the reference. Everything beneath the hide is dry alloy, cabling and woven filament — never wet, never organic, never red in substance.
SENSOR BAND STATES: the band glows DIM AMBER while walking, searching or observing. It snaps to HARD RED the instant the unit commits to violence and stays red until it stops. Nothing else on the machine ever emits light.
<<<9539a571-b86a-44ac-86ba-6c0c0d68b801>>>: a Mudhol hound, tall and lean, deep-chested, narrow-waisted, short fawn coat soaked flat and dripping, narrow muzzle, ribs showing, white flash on the chest, wearing ONLY a plaited rope collar with NOTHING attached. 100% matches the reference. A living animal — wet glossy eyes with clear bright catch-lights, visible breath vapour, mouth closed, individual wet hairs moving.
<<<7a5a8a4f-8af5-4e11-ab09-3738e138fb41>>>: twelve-metre-diameter precast concrete lining segments, ring after ring receding into total blackness, dry cable trays along both walls, twenty years of undisturbed pale dust, damp streaking and mineral bloom. Absolute black beyond thirty metres. 100% matches the reference.
<<<24af07af-e886-46a5-b3cf-5a3fc7374277>>>: a vertical shaft in the tunnel crown dropping a single hard column of sodium light onto the floor with rain falling its entire height, everything outside the column near-black. 100% matches the reference.

FORMAT MODE
Timed multishot. Five shots joined by four hard cuts. Cuts only at the specified points — the camera does not cut on its own.
0.0s SHOT A · 3.0s CUT · 3.0s SHOT B · 6.5s CUT · 6.5s SHOT C · 9.5s CUT · 9.5s SHOT D · 12.0s CUT · 12.0s SHOT E · ends 15.0s

OPTICS
A: WS down the empty bore, 63°. B: WS looking back, 63°. C: low WS, 63°. D: MCU on the hound, 29°. E: low WS through the light column, 63°. No drift mid-segment. Rectilinear throughout.

CAMERA
A — one metre above the floor, static and locked, looking back down the tunnel.
B — one metre above the floor, static and locked, identical framing to A.
C — twenty-five centimetres above the floor, static and locked.
D — forty centimetres above the floor, tracking alongside the hound at 15 km/h, tremor 3cm.
E — thirty centimetres above the floor, static and locked, the light column in the middle distance.

ACTION

SHOT A, 0.0–3.0s. In frame: <<<7a5a8a4f-8af5-4e11-ab09-3738e138fb41>>> only. Nothing else at all.
Looking back down the empty tunnel. No machines, no animals, no people. Pale dust hangs and settles. The travelling lamp glow recedes away behind camera so the frame darkens gradually. Nothing enters and nothing moves. Held on emptiness.

SHOT B, 3.0–6.5s. In frame: <<<f96bebed-11ad-4b5a-b563-75dda756d998>>> UNIT ONE and UNIT TWO, <<<7a5a8a4f-8af5-4e11-ab09-3738e138fb41>>>.
Identical framing to A. Two quadruped shapes resolve out of the blackness — and they are WALKING. A slow, steady, deliberate four-beat walk, one foot at a time, entirely unhurried. Their head pods stay dead level and do not bob with the stride, which no animal's head does. Both sensor bands glow DIM AMBER, two thin warm slots in the dark. They advance at walking pace and never break into a run. Then at 6.2 seconds, with no other change and no movement, UNIT ONE'S BAND SNAPS FROM AMBER TO HARD RED. It is still walking when it happens. Cut.

SHOT C, 6.5–9.5s. In frame: <<<f96bebed-11ad-4b5a-b563-75dda756d998>>>, low and close.
Both bands are now HARD RED and stay red. Without wind-up or warning both machines go from a walk to a FULL GALLOP in a single stride, closing on camera fast, dust exploding beneath them. At 8 seconds the lead unit leaves the ground entirely in a pounce — all four feet completely off the floor, segmented spine at full extension, forelegs thrown out ahead and hind legs driven out behind, airborne and travelling directly at the lens, its blank head pod level and pointed straight at camera with the red band burning. It fills frame as it comes.

SHOT D, 9.5–12.0s. In frame: <<<9539a571-b86a-44ac-86ba-6c0c0d68b801>>> only.
Close alongside the hound at full speed. He hears it. His head twists hard back over his right shoulder — ears swinging forward and up, neck stretched, the whites showing at the inner corners of his eyes. His body stays committed forward while his head is turned back. His eyes are wet and glossy with a bright catch-light in each and breath vapour pulses visibly from his nostrils. A faint red glow reaches him from behind and moves across his flank. He drops his head and runs harder.

SHOT E, 12.0–15.0s. In frame: all four of <<<f96bebed-11ad-4b5a-b563-75dda756d998>>>, <<<24af07af-e886-46a5-b3cf-5a3fc7374277>>>.
Low and static. All four come through the falling column of sodium light together, four abreast at full gallop, in wear order left to right — intact, worn, stripped, bare. All four sensor bands are HARD RED. For one second they are fully lit inside the column, rain running off hide and straight off bare alloy, four identical gaits moving in near-unison, four red slots burning in four blank heads. Then they come on out of it toward camera without slowing. One of them barks.

PERFORMANCE
The machines have no expression, no faces and no mouths at any point — the band is the only thing on them that changes, and it changes before they do. The walk carries no menace in its movement; it is simply unhurried. The charge begins with no crouch and no gather. Kempa is the only thing here that reacts to anything and the only thing that is alive.

PHYSICS
All four share one identical skeleton and gait whether covered or bare. Hard narrow feet strike dry dust and blow it outward. In the pounce the machine is genuinely airborne with real mass and arc. Rain falls only inside the column and runs straight off bare alloy, beading only on synthetic hide.

LIGHTING
In shots A to D the only standing light is the receding work-lamp glow from far behind camera, hard and falling off fast, so the machines emerge out of absolute black. From 6.2 seconds the red sensor bands become a second source — small, hard and directional, throwing a faint red wash forward onto dust and concrete ahead of each unit. In shot E the shaft's column of warm sodium at 3200K lights all four clearly.

COLOR GRADE
Grey concrete and pale dust, one warm lamp, one column of sodium, absolute black between them. Oxide-grey alloy, worn black-and-tan hide, braided grey cabling. The ONLY red in frame is the sensor bands and the faint wash they throw — never on flesh, never a wound, never blood.

AUDIO
Shot A is near-silent — dust settling, distant receding footsteps, the faint hum of the pod far ahead. In shot B, many hard alloy feet walking on concrete at a slow measured pace, echoing. There is no sound at all when the band turns red. At the cut to C the walking rhythm explodes instantly into a full gallop. Dog claws and hard breathing in D. In E, sixteen alloy feet at speed and one dog's bark — sharp, loud, convincing, with a faint speaker artefact, identical to every other bark in the film. No panting, no growling and no breathing from any unit.

STYLE
Photoreal live-action cinematic realism, anamorphic character, twenty-year-abandoned infrastructure, fine film grain.

OUTPUT SETTINGS
1080p HD, 16:9, real-time speed throughout, no slow motion.

POSITIVE LOCKS
Cuts happen only at 3.0, 6.5, 9.5 and 12.0 seconds. Shot A stays completely empty for its full three seconds. In shot B both units WALK at ordinary walking pace with a four-beat gait and level unmoving head pods, and never run — and their bands stay DIM AMBER until 6.2 seconds, when one and only one turns HARD RED while still walking. From shot C onward every band stays hard red. Every unit has a blank armoured head pod with one horizontal sensor band and NO face, NO muzzle, NO eyes and NO mouth. Everything beneath the hide is dry alloy, cabling and filament — never wet, never organic. The only red anywhere in frame is the sensor bands and their wash — no blood, no wounds and no red on any living thing. In shot E the four run in wear order from intact to bare. <<<9539a571-b86a-44ac-86ba-6c0c0d68b801>>> keeps wet eyes with catch-lights and visible breath, and nothing is attached to his collar. The bark is a recording, identical every time. No unit pants, growls or breathes.

THE FOUR VARIANTS, left to right across the sheet:
UNIT ONE — nearly intact. UNIT TWO — worn through. The hide has gone at both shoulders and across the haunches, exposing alloy and braided cabling in wide patches. What remains hangs loose at the belly and flank. The head pod is half bare.
UNIT THREE — mostly stripped. Only rags of hide remain, flapping at the neck and one thigh. The skeleton, the actuator bundles and the segmented spine are fully visible along the body.
UNIT FOUR — completely bare. No hide at all anywhere. Pure exposed machine: alloy skeleton, cabling, joint housings, the blank head pod with its lit sensor band. Heavily scored, rust-bloomed and repaired with mismatched plate at one shoulder.

SCENE CONTEXT
A tiny figure walks across black water toward a machine the size of a mountain range. The
machine tries to make him stop. It fails. By the end the heads have closed around him on every
side and the camera is looking straight down into the well they have made.

OUTPUT SETTINGS
IT IS NIGHT. Single continuous take, 10 seconds, real-time. The camera performs ONE continuous
move: it opens on the composition of REF A — water level, behind and above the figure, the heads
towering over him — and RISES AND PUSHES FORWARD over his head as he walks, climbing until it
arrives at the composition of REF B, looking almost straight down at him with the heads closed
in a ring. The references are for composition, scale, atmosphere and grade; they are not frames
to be matched pixel for pixel. No cuts, no zoom. Visible film grain. Only diegetic sound. No
dialogue.

highlights. Short wrapped garment, sleeveless vest, barefoot, the flute held loosely in his
right hand at his side. 100% matches the reference.

HIS PACE — this is the whole idea of the shot
He walks at one steady unhurried pace from the first second to the last. Every time the machine
moves at him, his stride does not change, his head does not turn, the flute does not lift. The
camera and the machine do everything; he does one thing.

 down, red points steady. Rain. The camera begins to rise.
0:02–0:04 THE FEINT. The nearest head on the left DROPS toward him fast — a strike that stops

 and shift. He keeps walking. The camera is now above him, still climbing.
0:06–0:08 THE CLOSING. All the heads lean inward at once from every side, the fanned hoods

 over the crown of his head, tilting down.
0:08–0:10 THE WELL. The camera settles high, looking down, as REF B. The heads have closed
 into a ring around him, hoods interlocked, red points in every direction, the amber
 at his feet the only light in the bottom. He is still walking forward into the dark
 at the centre.

His pace, posture and the flute never change. The camera move is one continuous physical
crane — real parallax as the columns slide past each other, never a zoom, never a cut. The
heads move with enormous mass: slow to start, fast at the end of the strike, a hard stop
with water shaken off and the whole column swaying after. Rain streaks, never dots — long
smears where the top light catches it; foreground drops cross the lens; two sit on the front
element. Specular breakup on the near plate, none on the far heads. The top light clips to
white and blooms; the red points clip at their cores; everything not lit falls to TRUE BLACK
with no recoverable detail. Coarse irregular 35mm grain heaviest in the haze. The camera
carries a faint drift. This is a live-action VFX plate, not a render. Palette: 60% grey haze
and black water, 30% rust and wet oxide plate, 6% white top light, 3% amber at his feet, 1%
red sensor points. The only blue is the rim highlight on his skin.

hood plates locking wider, water sheeting off and hitting the surface, his bare feet in shallow
water — steady, unchanging, four beats to the metre, audible under everything.
